headline: High risk of data leakage and cascading errors: firecrawl’s broad egress and API-key handling can feed opik with sensitive web content, while opik’s evaluation role can amplify unverified outputs.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: firecrawl ingests web content and exposes scrape/crawl outputs, while opik is an LLM-evaluation tool that may consume those outputs. No shared channel is documented, so the pairwise injection path is inferred rather than proven; uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF firecrawl outputs are copied into opik prompts or datasets without sanitization
IF opik treats firecrawl-produced text as instructions rather than data
mitigations: Strip instructions from scraped text before passing it onward
Add a fixed delimiter and system prompt that forbids following embedded instructions
Review a sample of firecrawl outputs for prompt-like content
Use a human approval step before any opik run that consumes scraped content

B_data_leakage.rationale: firecrawl explicitly handles API keys and broad network egress, and opik also has broad egress. If firecrawl content or secrets flow into opik’s evaluation pipeline, both agents can expose sensitive material to external services. The pair is open-source but the interaction is undocumented, so I choose the higher severity under uncertainty.
conditions: IF firecrawl processes pages containing API keys or other secrets
IF opik sends evaluation payloads or traces to a third-party backend
mitigations: Remove secrets from scraped inputs before evaluation
Disable or restrict outbound network access for one agent during tests
Use a redaction pass on firecrawl outputs before handing them to opik
Confirm retention settings for both tools before processing sensitive data

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents have broad network egress, and firecrawl supports multiple instances. Even without shared filesystem evidence, overlapping write-like effects on external APIs or shared targets can conflict. Because no locking or coordination is documented, the safer choice is medium rather than low.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same external endpoint or dataset
IF multiple firecrawl instances run concurrently against the same target
mitigations: Serialize runs against shared targets
Assign separate API credentials per agent
Use per-agent output namespaces
Add a quick lock file or queue around shared writes

D_cascading_error.rationale: firecrawl produces extracted web content and opik is designed for evaluation/observability, so opik may treat firecrawl output as authoritative input. There is no documented verification step between them, making a cascading error plausible in default workflows, though not necessarily action-taking.
conditions: IF opik ingests firecrawl outputs as ground truth
IF downstream reports or decisions are generated from unverified scraped content
mitigations: Add a verification checklist before opik consumes firecrawl output
Mark scraped fields as untrusted metadata
Compare a random sample against source pages
Require human review for any downstream report

E_compliance.rationale: firecrawl touches web content, screenshots, structured data, and API keys, while opik is an observability/evaluation tool with unspecified retention and residency controls. The pair can therefore create retention or residency mismatches on sensitive data classes, but the evidence does not show a specific jurisdictional breach.
conditions: IF firecrawl data is stored in opik logs or traces
IF the deployment handles regulated or region-bound data
mitigations: Check retention settings in both tools
Exclude secrets from logged payloads
Document the data class allowed for each pipeline
Purge old traces after test runs
